english: How goods move between settlement stores. These are fixed for the life of a campaign: change them from the main menu before starting a new one. In a multiplayer campaign they are ignored and every value is the default on every machine. The recruitment and replenishment settings, the trade route lines and the Vanilla supply lines box can be changed at any time.

english: How many resources a recruit takes from your stores for each 100 gold it is worth. 0 turns this off. You can change this during a campaign. The change applies from your next turn.
old_english: How many resources a recruit takes from your stores for each 100 gold it is worth. 0 turns this off.

english: Strength a unit regains takes resources from your stores, as a share of what recruiting it takes: at 100, a unit that regains half its strength takes half its recruit's resources. What your stores cannot pay for is paid in gold when Gold pays for troops is ticked, and is lost again when it is not. 0 turns this off. You can change this during a campaign. The change applies from your next turn.
old_english: Strength a unit regains takes resources from your stores, as a share of what recruiting it takes: at 100, a unit that regains half its strength takes half its recruit's resources. Strength your stores cannot pay for is lost again. 0 turns this off.

english: Every unit you recruit takes resources from your stores by its type and worth (cavalry and monsters take mounts, infantry and war machines take war materials, the finest also take your rare resource). What the stores lack is paid in your race's own currency where it has one. A recruit whose resources are still short arrives understrength, unless Gold pays for troops is ticked. Vampire Counts and Vampire Coast recruits take nothing. Off: recruiting takes nothing. You can change this during a campaign. The change applies from your next turn.
old_english: Every unit you recruit takes resources from your stores by its type and worth (cavalry and monsters take mounts, infantry and war machines take war materials, the finest also take your rare resource). What the stores lack is paid in your race's own currency where it has one. A recruit whose resources are still short arrives understrength, unless Gold pays for recruits is ticked. Vampire Counts and Vampire Coast recruits take nothing. Off: recruiting takes nothing.

english: What your stores and your race's currency cannot cover is paid in gold, for recruits and for replenishing alike. Off: a recruit arrives understrength instead and must regain the rest by replenishing, and strength a unit regains that your stores cannot pay for is lost again. A faction no player controls always pays in gold. You can change this during a campaign. The change applies from your next turn.
